pages.title: Repository Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to @queenanya/baileys — what it is, its architecture, key capabilities, and how the major subsystems relate. Links to all child sections for deeper reading.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for installing the library, meeting Node.js ≥20 requirements, initializing makeWASocket, handling QR/pairing-code authentication, and wiring up the event emitter for a minimal working bot.

pages.title: Configuration Reference
pages.purpose: Detailed reference for SocketConfig / UserFacingSocketConfig options: auth state, logger (Pino), browser identity, keepAlive, media cache, cache backends, and all tunable parameters.

pages.title: Connection & Authentication
pages.purpose: Overview of how the library establishes and maintains a secure connection to WhatsApp servers, covering the Noise Protocol handshake, credential lifecycle, and multi-device pairing. Links to child pages for details.

pages.title: WebSocket & Noise Protocol Handshake
pages.purpose: Deep dive into makeSocket and the WebSocketClient: how the Noise Protocol XX handshake is performed, frame encoding/decoding, keep-alive pings, connection teardown, and the event-buffer optimization for offline message processing.

pages.title: Authentication State & Credential Management
pages.purpose: Explains AuthenticationCreds, SignalKeyStore, and the three auth-state backends (useMultiFileAuthState, useSingleFileAuthState, useMongoFileAuthState). Covers initAuthCreds, addTransactionCapability, makeCacheableSignalKeyStore, and how to persist keys correctly to avoid decryption errors.

pages.title: Device Pairing & Registration
pages.purpose: Covers QR-code pairing vs. pairing-code flow, generateRegistrationNode, generateLoginNode, configureSuccessfulPairing, ADVSignedDeviceIdentity HMAC verification, and pre-key upload lifecycle.

pages.title: Messaging Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the full message pipeline from high-level sendMessage calls down to encrypted binary stanzas, and from incoming stanzas up to typed WAMessage events. Links to child pages for send, receive, and content construction.

pages.title: Sending Messages
pages.purpose: Detailed coverage of makeMessagesSocket: sendMessage, relayMessage, createParticipantNodes, getUSyncDevices, assertSessions, the encryption mutex, LID-priority logic, sender-key distribution for groups, newsletter plaintext path, TC Token, and media retry flow.

pages.title: Receiving Messages & Incoming Stanzas
pages.purpose: Covers makeMessagesRecvSocket: CB:message / CB:receipt / CB:notification / CB:call handlers, decryption retry lifecycle, offline batch processing, newsletter MEX notifications, identity-change handling, and the processingMutex.

pages.title: Message Content Construction
pages.purpose: Explains generateWAMessage, generateWAMessageContent, prepareWAMessageMedia, the media encryption/upload pipeline (encryptedStream, fileEncSha256, mediaKey), link-preview generation, poll versioning, contextInfo/quoting, and getBizBinaryNode for interactive messages.

pages.title: Rich & Interactive Messages
pages.purpose: Documents the rich message composer: generateTableContent, generateListContent, generateCodeBlockContent, generateLatexContent, generateMarkdownContent, generateRichMessageContent, botForwardedMessage, unifiedResponse UX primitives, nativeFlow buttons, carousel, and interactive templates.

pages.title: End-to-End Encryption & Signal Protocol
pages.purpose: Overview of the cryptographic stack: Signal Protocol sessions, group sender keys, LID migration, and app-state LTHash. Links to child pages for the Signal layer and app-state sync.

pages.title: Signal Session Management
pages.purpose: Covers libsignal integration, SignalRepository, pre-key generation and upload, session creation/migration from PN to LID, the Group sender-key sub-system (SenderKeyRecord, GroupSessionBuilder, GroupCipher), and the encryptionMutex pattern.

pages.title: App-State Sync & LTHash
pages.purpose: Explains the app-state synchronization system: SyncAction patches, CollectionName buckets (REGULAR, CRITICAL_BLOCK, etc.), LTHash differential verification, resyncAppState, and how settings/contacts/chat metadata are mutated across devices.

pages.title: Protocol Buffers (WAProto)
pages.purpose: Overview of the WAProto directory: how .proto files are organized, generated, and consumed. Links to child pages covering the major proto namespaces.

pages.title: Proto Extraction & Generation Pipeline
pages.purpose: Documents the automated scripts/index.js pipeline: scraping WhatsApp Web service worker for client_revision, AST parsing with acorn to extract internalSpec/internalDefaults, cross-reference resolution, .proto file generation, pbts TypeScript declaration generation, and the GitHub Actions workflow schedule.

pages.title: E2E & Web Message Schemas
pages.purpose: Reference for the core proto namespaces: E2E.proto (all message content types, polls, events, AI messages, LIDMigrationMappingSyncMessage), Web.proto (WebMessageInfo lifecycle, MessageAddOn, KeepInChat, PollUpdate, WebFeatures), and MdStorageMsgRowOpaqueData (flat storage schema).

pages.title: History Sync, AI, & Auxiliary Protos
pages.purpose: Covers HistorySync.proto (history sync types, progress tracking), AICommon.proto (AI query/response structures), AICommonDeprecated, SyncAction.proto (full mutation catalog), StatusAttributions, CompanionReg, DeviceCapabilities, Adv, Cert, Ephemeral, and other auxiliary proto packages.

pages.title: Socket Layer & Feature Modules
pages.purpose: Overview of the Socket directory's layered composition pattern and the feature-specific socket modules. Links to child pages for groups/communities, newsletters, business, and USync.

pages.title: Groups & Communities
pages.purpose: Documents makeGroupsSocket and makeCommunitiesSocket: group creation, participant management (add/remove/promote/demote), invite codes (V3/V4), ephemeral settings, join-approval mode, member-add mode, community-linked groups, and extractGroupMetadata binary parsing.

pages.title: Newsletters (Channels)
pages.purpose: Covers makeNewsletterSocket: creating, following, muting, and deleting newsletters; admin management (adminCount, changeOwner, demote); fetching messages and updates; reaction modes; MEX/GraphQL queries for newsletter metadata; and newsletter-specific incoming notification handling.

pages.title: Business, Chats & Profile
pages.purpose: Documents business socket methods (getCatalog, productCreate/Update/Delete, getBusinessProfile), chat management (chatModify, star, clearMessage, labels), privacy settings (updateLastSeenPrivacy, updateOnlinePrivacy, etc.), profile updates, and the chats socket (appPatch, resyncAppState, cleanDirtyBits).

pages.title: USync Protocol & Username System
pages.purpose: Explains the USync (Universal Sync) protocol: USyncQuery builder, USyncUser, all protocol handlers (Contact, LID, Device, Status, Username, BotProfile, DisappearingMode), executeUSyncQuery, and the username socket (checkUsername, setUsername, findUserByUsername) via Mex/GraphQL.

pages.title: VoIP & Voice Calls
pages.purpose: Overview of the VoIP subsystem and call signaling. Links to child pages for the WASM engine and the call signaling/transport layer.

pages.title: WASM Engine & PThread Pool
pages.purpose: Deep dive into WasmEngine (wasm-engine.mjs): loading whatsapp.wasm in a vm.Context, the 20-worker PThread pool using SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics proxy to prevent event-loop blocking, the custom module registry (__d/require), initVoipStack, audio capture (PCM 16kHz/Mono/Float32 via malloc/sendAudioData), and audio playback loop.

pages.title: VoipClient, Signaling & Transport
pages.purpose: Covers VoipClient lifecycle (connect, initWithSocket, call), SignalingBridge (offer/accept/terminate/transport stanzas), RelayRtcTransport for media relay, AudioFeeder, TC Token requirement, LID/PN resolution for calls, and the call signaling flow in makeMessagesRecvSocket (offerCall, acceptCall, terminateCall, sendTransport).

pages.title: State Management & Storage
pages.purpose: Overview of how the library manages in-memory and persistent state. Links to child pages for the in-memory store, anti-delete, and the WABinary encoding layer.

pages.title: In-Memory Store & Cache Backends
pages.purpose: Documents makeInMemoryStore (bind, loadMessages, writeToFile/readFromFile, KeyedDB ordering), makeCacheManagerStore, makeOrderedDictionary, ObjectRepository, and how the store reacts to BaileysEventEmitter events (messaging-history.set, chats.upsert, messages.upsert, group-participants.update).

pages.title: Anti-Delete & Message Retention
pages.purpose: Explains the MessageStore class: storeMessage with maxMessagesPerChat eviction, TTL-based cleanup, markAsDeleted, createAntiDeleteHandler listening for REVOKE protocol messages, and the deletedMessages recovery map.
